learnings.claim: Shopify's official API limits page (fetched 2026-10-09) says most limits use a leaky bucket whose size and restore rate depend on API and plan, recommends a one-second backoff after throttling, caps array inputs at 250 items on every API, and caps pagination at 25,000 objects including count queries.
learnings.decision: SHOPIFY_BUCKET_GATE: shopify_client must back off at least 1 s on throttle, chunk any array input to <=250, and treat a 25,000-object page walk as truncated (switch to bulk operations) instead of reporting complete counts.
fallback_history: Without store credentials, unit-test chunking and backoff with recorded fixtures only.
learnings.next_measurement: When store credentials exist, log extensions.cost.throttleStatus per call and count throttle events per run.
learnings.title: Shopify leaky-bucket backoff and hard caps

learnings.claim: The official GraphQL Admin API reference (fetched 2026-10-09) states that the GraphQL API can return 200 OK for cases that would be 4xx/5xx in REST, with errors[].extensions.code values such as THROTTLED, ACCESS_DENIED, SHOP_INACTIVE and INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR, that a single query above the max cost (1000) fails with MAX_COST_EXCEEDED, and that responses carry extensions.cost.throttleStatus.
learnings.decision: SHOPIFY_200_ERROR_GATE: never treat HTTP 200 as success; a response with a non-empty errors array or mutation userErrors is a failure classified by extensions.code. THROTTLED -> backoff/retry; MAX_COST_EXCEEDED -> split query or use bulk operation; ACCESS_DENIED/SHOP_INACTIVE -> stop and escalate to Furkan.
fallback_history: If Admin API access is blocked, use Shopify admin CSV exports as a manual fallback and mark data user_reported.
learnings.next_measurement: Add a fixture test for each code once a real error sample is captured from the store.
learnings.title: Shopify GraphQL errors arrive with HTTP 200
